title: Anatomy of a signed News container
body: Everything your console downloads from OpenPak News arrives as a BCAT container: a 288-byte header, then the payload. The header carries a fresh random counter block, an encrypted body and an RSA-2048 signature computed over the plaintext, so the console verifies what it read, not just what it received. Our encoder builds exactly that shape: PKCS#1 signatures with SHA-256, AES-CTR encryption, and no platform secrets anywhere in the source. The same container format serves the catalog, channel details and, once validated, articles.
